thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected for model-service (us-west-2). Autoscaler generated multiple scale events in last 4m. Pager triggered for oncall. See incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042 (auto-created)

ops-oncall: on it. assigning to @sanjay and @maya. can we get current impact numbers? 

sanjay: p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 950ms, 5xxs ~ 18% over 3m. A lot of CUDA OOMs in the runtime logs. stack snippets below. 

sanjay: ```
E0321 14:02:10.123 runtime.cpp:274] CUDA out of memory when allocating 856 MB. free=512MB total=16384MB
E0321 14:02:10.124 kv_cache.cpp:97] failed to allocate KV cache page at 0x7f8d...
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what(): std::bad_alloc
```

maya: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down within seconds. looks like node-provisioner added nodes, pods scheduled, then OOM/crashlooped which caused downscale. volume of events = thrash. excerpt: 

maya: ```
I0321 14:01:58 autoscaler.go:410] scaling up target=45 current=12 (reason: queued 30)
I0321 14:02:03 autoscaler.go:520] scaling down target=18 current=40 (reason: crashloop/pod eviction)
```

leah: guess: aggressive scale policies + model-serving staying on GPU heavy quant profile. when nodes come up pods try to use full allocation -> OOM -> evict -> autoscaler sees low ready -> spins again. repeat.

jordan: cs-rep flagged 3 enterprise customers reporting timeouts in last 10 mins (acme-co, helios-ai, mycraft). they're seeing request retries and some 5xx traces. notif sent to reps.

ops-oncall: we need quick mitigation to stop thrash and reduce customer impact. proposals: 1) increase autoscaler stabilization window to 3m, 2) reduce max replicas temporarily, 3) pin a fallback model variant (cpu-quant-small) for new requests, 4) disable aggressive scale-to-zero. thoughts? 

sanjay: +1 to stabilization window and cap replicas. doing a quick runtime config patch now. will also toggle fallback to cpu for non-enterprise traffic to preserve dedicated GPU quota for long-running sessions.

devops-bot: COMMAND: kubectl patch hpa model-service -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleUp": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 180}, "scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 180}}}}' --namespace prod

leah: also lowering model batch_size to 4 and max_tokens 1024 on the GPU variant until we get stable nodes. patching config map.

ops-oncall: applying replica cap to 30 to prevent runaway scale.

devops-bot: COMMAND: kubectl scale deployment/model-service --replicas=30 --namespace prod

maya: I'm seeing OOM rate drop after batch_size change, but still a few crashloops on older nodes with mixed drivers. suspect some nodes still have older CUDA driver causing memory fragmentation. flagged infra to cordon those nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-az3-07`

infra (via devops-bot): Cordon issued for gpu-node-az3-07 and gpu-node-az3-09. draining scheduled.

cs-rep: sending interim customer status: "We're aware of increased errors and actively mitigating; targeted ETA 30-45m for restore of baseline latency." cc: @jordan

ops-oncall: summary so far: immediate mitigations applied: - autoscaler stabilization window 180s - replica cap 30 - fallback CPU variant for new traffic - reduced batch_size on GPU variant - cordoned suspect GPU nodes

ops-oncall: impact: partial degradation for some enterprise customers, overall error rate down from 18% -> 6% after changes but latency still elevated for long-tail requests.

sanjay: logging action: collect node-level GPU utilization + dmesg from cordoned nodes and attach to incident. suspect driver/kernel mismatch. also capture runtime OOM traces for postmortem.

maya: assigning follow-ups: @leah to validate driver versions across pool, @sanjay to prepare rollback plan for autoscaler policy, @ops-oncall to coordinate next 30m handoff to night oncall if still unstable. I'll continue watching.

ops-oncall: handing off to night-oncall @kevin at 14:06 UTC. brief: autoscale thrash triggered by repeated GPU OOMs causing crashloops -> autoscaler oscillation -> brownout. mitigations applied as above. watchlist: error rate, node driver mismatch, pending pod eviction loops.

kevin: acked. please paste docs + logs into the incident page and add me as responder. I'll take over monitoring and kick off postmortem template if we don't hit steady state in 2 hours. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager cleared for primary oncall. Incident still open. Incident channel created: #incident-1739123456. Postmortem owner: kevin.

ops-oncall: adding quick runbook snippet for mitigation in case it spikes again: 

ops-oncall: ```
# quick mitigations
1) kubectl patch hpa model-service to set stabilizationWindowSeconds=180
2) kubectl scale deployment/model-service --replicas=30
3) patch ConfigMap model-config: set batch_size=4 for gpu variant
4) kubectl cordon <suspect-node> and drain
5) route new non-enterprise traffic to cpu-fallback via routing policy
```

kevin: logged. will trigger escalation to infra if cordoned nodes don't drain cleanly. I'll update timeline in incident page.

jordan: will follow up with CS to escalate to the 3 impacted customers and offer targeted retries/SL credits if SLA impacted.

leah: noted for postmortem: include autoscaler policy tuning, runtime memory accounting, and driver validation gating in our node autoscaling pipeline.

ops-oncall: closing thread here for live chat. all updates to incident page. thanks everyone. :heart:
